classification.difficultyReason: Apply the triangle area rule twice and explain equal areas using supplementary-angle sine values.

content.prompt: Find the area of these two triangles, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Triangle with vertical left side, lower side sloping upwards to the right, and an included 60-degree angle. Ordinary source blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent sides are 20 cm and 15 cm; their included angle is 60 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle with vertical left side and lower side sloping downwards to the right. An arrow connects the 120-degree label to its included angle arc. Ordinary source blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent sides are 20 cm and 15 cm; their included angle is 120 degrees.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What do you notice? How can you explain this?

answer.worked: Both triangles have the same two given side lengths. Since $120^\circ=180^\circ-60^\circ$ and $\sin(180^\circ-\theta)=\sin\theta$, the included angles have equal sine values. Therefore, $A=\frac12 ab\sin C$ gives equal areas.
